title: Stdout markers, prompt lines and the derived outcome
description: Contract C5. The engine prints markers, the daemon reads them. The process exit code is never a signal: both providers exit zero even for a failed run, a denied tool and a blocked stop. The outcome is derived from on-disk gate state first, the marker second, denials third.

marker_line.description: The last non-empty assistant line of a driver turn.

prompt_line.description: The first line the daemon sends when it resumes a driver. Every kind ends with a measured `at=` on the A6 form, so a resumed driver never carries a time forward or formats one.

prompt_gate_answer.description: An operator answered a pending gate; `at=` is when the answer was given.

prompt_re_drive.description: The daemon re-enters a driver that owes another turn; `at=` is when the re-drive was issued.

prompt_steer.description: An operator steers a running driver with free text; `at=` is when the steer was sent.

prompt_resume.description: A plain re-entry carrying neither an answer nor an instruction; `at=` is when the resume was issued.

outcome.description: What the daemon records for one driver turn.

denials.description: Denied tool calls harvested from the provider's own record. A non-empty list marks the turn incomplete whatever the model claimed.
